assumptions: Assay platforms (capture reagents, particle counters, omics) are available at participating sites and can be harmonized with SOPs.
Sufficient pilot GMP-like lots can be produced and aliquoted for blinded distribution.
Exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer with orthogonal readout is available and behaves comparably across labs.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 and program rodent evidence highlight that orthogonal, membrane-protection–based identity signals are necessary to attribute activity to intact EVs and to enable meaningful lot-to-lot comparisons. Demonstrating reproducibility of a composite fingerprint across independent pilot lots and analytical sites, with spike-in controls to exclude assay failure, would permit a qualitative comparability gate without asserting numeric release criteria.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative presence/absence of composite fingerprint across capture-positive particle-peak fractions; binary pass/fail comparability call.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Composite lot-comparability fingerprint (qualitative)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: A composite, non-numeric fingerprint combining orthogonal intact-EV identity and protected-cargo signals can enable a qualitative comparability gate without premature numeric release limits if it is reproducibly measurable across pilot lots and sites.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: depends on assay harmonization, spike-in performance, and true lot consistency.

edges.competing_explanation: Reproducible assay readouts could reflect consistent co-isolation of non-vesicular components or site-specific assay harmonization rather than true EV-associated fingerprint conservation.
edges.missing_experiment: A blinded, multi-lot, multi-site study with spike-in controls, harmonized SOPs, and a predefined qualitative scoring rubric to separate assay reproducibility from sample consistency.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal fingerprints and program rodent studies motivate identity linkage, but program-specific reproducibility across sites is untested.

edges.competing_explanation: Discordant site calls may result from logistical factors (cold-chain deviations, shipping) rather than true lack of fingerprint conservation.
edges.missing_experiment: Controlled blinded shipments with stability/chain-of-custody records and spike-in recovery monitoring to isolate shipping effects.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: large-animal biodistribution uncertainty elevates the need for robust comparability gates, but lack of reproducibility could reflect true lot variability or limitations in the candidate fingerprint.

nodes.statement: An orthogonal composite fingerprint (A: capture-positive surface-marker signal co-localized with particle-count peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity; B: protected-cargo multi-omic pattern in capture-positive fractions; C: consistent particle:protein context) is measurable in bounded EV-enriched fractions when intact EVs are present and membranes are preserved.

If the composite fingerprint can be measured reproducibly across >=3 pilot lots and >=2 analytical sites under blinded conditions with spike-in recovery controls, then the fingerprint can serve as a qualitative lot-comparability gate (non-numeric) for advancing lots into bridging studies.

If the fingerprint is not reproducible across lots or sites (discordant qualitative calls) despite validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls, then lot-to-lot variability remains unresolved and the program cannot rely on the fingerprint for comparability decisions.

competing_explanations: Concordant fingerprint detection could reflect consistent co-isolation of non-vesicular complexes rather than EV-associated signals.
Discordant results could reflect shipping/cold-chain failures or site assay variability rather than inherent lot differences.
dependencies: Produce >=3 pilot GMP-like lots and aliquot under chain-of-custody for blinded distribution
Select and qualify >=2 analytical laboratories and harmonize SOPs
Obtain or produce a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer with orthogonal detection
design_question: Can a blinded, multi-lot, multi-site study using an exogenous intact-EV spike-in plus a predefined qualitative scoring rubric demonstrate reproducible detection of a composite orthogonal fingerprint (capture-positive surface phenotype co-localized with particle peaks, protected-cargo pattern, and particle:protein context) across pilot lots and sites so the fingerprint can be used as a non-numeric comparability gate without becoming a premature numeric release specification?
expected_measurable_effect: A reproducible qualitative fingerprint call (yes/no) per lot across analytical sites: capture-positive particle-peak co-localization with detergent/protease-sensitive capture signal; protected-cargo multi-omic presence in captured fractions; and consistent particle:protein context. Concordant calls across sites enable a pass (fingerprint reproducible) decision to advance lots into bridging studies.

experiment.assay: Blinded orthogonal workflow at each site: (A) fractionation to identify particle-peak fractions and particle counts per fraction; (B) intact immuno-capture ELISA/bead-capture for canonical surface markers on fractions; (C) detergent + protease/RNase protection test on captured material; (D) targeted protected-cargo assays (small-RNA panel + targeted proteomics) on capture-positive fractions; (E) total protein and particle:protein ratio per fraction. Sites use harmonized SOPs and report a binary fingerprint-present/fingerprint-absent call per lot plus raw data.
experiment.comparator: Blinded inter-site comparison: per lot, compare qualitative fingerprint calls across analytical sites. Positive control: characterized small-EV reference material included blinded at each site. Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted aliquots.
experiment.control: At each analytical site: (1) spike-in recovery readout per fraction (must be recovered and detergent/protease-sensitive), (2) characterized small-EV positive control processed blinded, (3) buffer-only negative control, and capture-compatibility buffer checks.
dependencies: Production of >=3 pilot GMP-like lots with split aliquots and cold-chain documentation
Availability of an orthogonal intact-EV spike-in tracer and harmonized SOPs
Two or more analytical labs with required orthogonal assay capabilities
experiment.failure_criterion: Discordant fingerprint calls across sites for the same lot despite validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls, or findings showing that apparent concordance is driven solely by spike-in recovery with absent endogenous fingerprint signals.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criterion is met, the hypothesis is falsified: the composite fingerprint is not robust enough across sites/lots to serve as a non-numeric comparability gate. The program should (A) avoid using this fingerprint for lot advancement decisions, (B) investigate assay harmonization or alternative attributes (tighter fractionation, protected-cargo panels), or (C) consider secretome-centric strategies.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A composite orthogonal fingerprint (capture-positive surface-marker co-localized with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive signal; protected-cargo multi-omic pattern in capture-positive fractions; and consistent particle:protein context) will be reproducibly observed across >=3 pilot GMP-like lots and >=2 analytical sites under blinded conditions when an exogenous intact-EV spike-in validates assay recovery, enabling a qualitative comparability pass/fail decision.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative reproducibility call per lot across sites (fingerprint reproducible = same qualitative pass/fail across all sites). Requirement: spike-in tracer recovery and protection behavior must validate assays at each site.
experiment.question: Can a blinded, multi-lot, multi-site study using an exogenous intact-EV spike-in and a predefined qualitative rubric reproducibly detect the composite fingerprint across pilot lots and sites, enabling a non-numeric comparability gate?
required_material: >=3 pilot GMP-like production lots aliquoted into blinded split-aliquots (cold-chain tracked)
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) to add to each aliquot pre-shipment

Harmonized SOPs for fractionation (SEC or iodixanol cushion), particle counting (NTA/TRPS), intact immuno-capture (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5), detergent+protease protection, and protected-cargo targeted assays
Particle-counter instruments and consumables at each site (NTA or TRPS)
Targeted small-RNA panel and targeted proteomics reagents with spike-in controls
secondary_readouts: Per-site spike-in recovery percentage and detergent/protease-sensitivity
Protected-cargo panel presence/absence concordance across sites
experiment.success_criterion: In blinded testing of >=3 pilot lots across >=2 analytical sites, each lot yields the same qualitative fingerprint call at all sites (concordant pass or concordant fail) and spike-in recovery & capture-compatibility controls confirm assay performance. Achieving concordant 'fingerprint reproducible' calls for >=2 lots (preferably all >=3) permits adopting the fingerprint as a qualitative comparability gate.

explicit_inferences: Inference: Spike-in–controlled, blinded multi-site measurement is required to separate assay robustness from true lot-to-lot fingerprint reproducibility.
Inference: A non-numeric, qualitative comparability gate reduces risk of premature numeric specifications while enabling manufacturing advancement decisions.
falsification_criteria: Discordant qualitative fingerprint calls across analytical sites for the same lot despite validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls (i.e., no reproducible composite fingerprint across >=3 lots and >=2 sites).
Observed concordance attributable to assay artifact or spike-in-only recovery rather than endogenous signal (controls show spike-in recovered but endogenous signals absent).
human_decisions_required: Approve pilot-lot production and blinded split/shipment plan
Select participating analytical sites and finalize harmonized SOPs and qualitative scoring rubric
Authorize procurement/production of exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and positive reference material
manufacturability_assessment: Feasible: requires production of >=3 pilot GMP-like lots with aliquoting and blinded split; costs/time for multi-site logistics and orthogonal omics increase resource needs but are appropriate for a Stage-1 comparability gate.
manufacturing_rationale: Manufacturing currently lacks representative lots and reproducible analytics. A blinded multi-site study using pilot GMP-like lots and a spike-in tracer verifies both production consistency and assay robustness across laboratories, de-risking premature numeric specifications while providing an operational go/no-go comparability decision for Stage-1 bridging runs.
measurement_strategy: Blinded split-sample distribution to >=2 analytical sites with harmonized SOPs, spike-in tracer added pre-aliquot; qualitative scoring rubric predefined (fingerprint present = pass if all three composite elements are observed and spike-in recovered), with capture-compatibility and spike-in controls at each site.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis requires a blinded, multi-site reproducibility study that combines an exogenous intact-EV spike-in (to control for assay recovery), a predefined qualitative pass/fail rubric, and split blinded pilot-lot distribution to separate assay robustness from true lot-level fingerprint conservation. Prior program proposals described multi-site fingerprinting but did not couple a spike-in–controlled, blinded inter-lab design with a predefined qualitative rubric as the decisive discriminating experiment; this controlled, blinded, multi-site spike-in approach is novel and directly addresses the lot-comparability evidence gap.
principal_risks: Assay harmonization failure across labs leading to false discordance.
Spike-in tracer behaves differently from endogenous EVs, limiting interpretability.
Pilot lot production variability too high to permit a reproducible fingerprint even if assays are robust.
proposed_potency_relationship: None asserted. The fingerprint is an identity/comparability gate; any linkage to potency will be explored in later, separate mechanism-linked experiments.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a non-numeric lot-comparability fingerprint (spike-in-validated capture-positive surface-phenotype co-localized with particle peaks; protected-cargo multi-omic pattern in capture-positive fractions; and consistent particle:protein context) as a pass/fail comparability gate for advancing pilot lots into bridging studies, contingent on blinded multi-site reproducibility.
title: Blinded multi-site spike-in–controlled fingerprint reproducibility for non-numeric lot-comparability gate
